letters.note: Sans: a sharp corner. Serif: a beak at the top-right and a tapering leg. By hand: often one curved stroke.
Sans: a symmetric tent. Serif: the left stroke grows a beak and leans. By hand: more like a check mark.
The top: a flat bar in Gothic, a slanted beaked stroke in Myeongjo, often a separate slash by hand.
The top mark is a short horizontal in Gothic, but a slanted dash or dot in serif and handwriting.
The 'hat' is a flat line in Gothic, a slanted stroke or dot in Myeongjo, and often a little loop by hand.
Sans: a tidy table. Serif: the two legs taper and pick up beaks at the feet.
The joints square off in print but round into a single squiggle in handwriting.
Stable overall — but serif adds small beaks to the end of each of the three bars.
